extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and disciplinary enforcement authorities
extracted.subtask_description: An official USPTO Final Order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 based on a state suspension, describing service, notice, findings, scope of suspension, and ancillary requirements (e.g., dissociation from customer numbers, duty compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for reciprocal discipline (statutory/regulatory basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Action taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 as the statutory and regulatory authority to impose reciprocal discipline based on a state suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for USPTO discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being suspended for two years from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO imposed suspension because the practitioner was suspended by the Nevada Supreme Court; the Order states the USPTO discipline is 'predicated upon being suspended for two years from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice procedure (37 C.F.R. § 11.35(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempted service by certified first-class mail to known addresses; when mail was undeliverable, service by publication in the Official Gazette for two consecutive weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office attempted certified mail service (receipt nos. given); one mailing returned 'Return to Sender' and the other was undeliverable, so the OED Director served Respondent by publication in the Official Gazette (March 15 and March 22, 2016). The published notice informed Respondent he could request a copy of the Notice and Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent had an opportunity to file a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent did not file a response. The Order states that because of the failure to file, 'there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)', supporting imposition of reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination standard when respondent fails to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response, there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), and reciprocal discipline identical to the state discipline is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Analysis section explicitly ties Respondent's failure to respond to the legal conclusion that suspension is appropriate; this describes the procedural/evidentiary effect of non-response under § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and duration of reciprocal suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for two years, effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order imposes discipline 'identical to' the state-imposed suspension: two years, and explicitly states the scope includes patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension, reasons for discipline, and referencing the state proceedings and rules violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the full text of the required Official Gazette notice (covering registration number, summary of Nevada findings, list of violated Nevada Rules of Professional Conduct, and reference to OED FOIA Reading Room).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs broad external notification consistent with § 11.59 to inform relevant authorities and the public about the discipline and its reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Order does not recite § 11.58's duties, it expressly requires Respondent to comply with them as part of the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure ('PKI') certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an operational consequence of discipline: the practitioner’s association with Customer Numbers and PKI certificates will be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to USPTO Customer Numbers until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for, obtain, or have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order expressly bars any new or continued association with Customer Numbers during the suspension period and until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying state misconduct findings and violated professional rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Nevada Supreme Court found by clear and convincing evidence that Respondent violated Rules 1.1 (competence); 1.3 (diligence); 1.4 (communication); 1.15 (safekeeping property); 5.5 (unauthorized practice of law); 8.1 (bar admission and disciplinary matters); and 8.4 (misconduct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order summarizes Nevada's factual findings: practicing while administratively suspended for failure to meet CLE, swearing in court documents that he was a licensed attorney, failing to competently and diligently pursue a personal injury matter, failing to communicate with clients, failing to respond to the State Bar, and failing to appear at disciplinary hearing. The Nevada court required suspension for two years and payment of costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions (OED FOIA Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides a link: http://efoia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp and directs publication and public access of the decision.
